==Problem ==
Haruki has a piece of wire that is <imath>24</imath> centimeters long. He wants to bend it to form each of the following shapes, one at a time:

A regular hexagon with side length <imath>5</imath> cm.

A square with area <imath>36 \hspace{3pt} \text{cm}^2</imath>.

A right triangle whose legs are <imath>6</imath> and <imath>8</imath> cm long.

Which of the shapes can Haruki make?

<imath>\textbf{(A)} \hspace{3pt} \text{Triangle only} \\ \textbf{(B)} \hspace{3pt} \text{Hexagon and square only} \\ \textbf{(C)} \hspace{3pt} \text{Hexagon and triangle only} \\  \textbf{(D)} \hspace{3pt} \text{Square and triangle only} \\ \textbf{(E)} \hspace{3pt} \text{Hexagon, triangle, and square}</imath>

==Solution 1==

	To solve this problem we can find the perimeter of each of the given spaces and check if it is less than 24.

The first shape is a regular hexagon with side length <imath>5</imath>. The hexagon has a perimeter of <imath>6 \cdot 5 = 30</imath> centimeters. The second shape is a square with area <imath>36</imath> or a side length of <imath>6</imath>. Then the perimeter of all <imath>4</imath> sides is <imath>24</imath> centimeters. Finally, we need to find the perimeter of a right triangle with legs <imath>6</imath> and <imath>8</imath> centimeters. The hypotenuse of the right triangle is <imath>10</imath> so the total perimeter is <imath>6 + 8 + 10 = 24</imath> centimeters.

Thus, only the square and the triangle can be made with 24 centimeters of wire so the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf {(D) } \text{Square and triangle only}}</imath>.

~ LogicalRhino65

==Solution 2 (Easy and simple, no need to know the sides of the triangle!)==

First, consider the regular hexagon. A regular hexagon with side length <imath>5</imath> cm has perimeter
<imath>6\cdot 5 = 30</imath> cm, which exceeds the available <imath>24</imath> cm of wire. Therefore, the hexagon cannot be formed, eliminating answer choices <imath>\textbf{(B)}</imath>, <imath>\textbf{(C)}</imath>, and <imath>\textbf{(E)}</imath>.

Next, consider the square. A square with area <imath>36\text{ cm}^2</imath> has side length <imath>\sqrt{36}=6</imath> cm, so its perimeter is
<imath>4\cdot 6 = 24</imath> cm. Thus, the square can be formed.

At this point, the only remaining answer choices are <imath>\textbf{(A)}</imath> and <imath>\textbf{(D)}</imath>. But since <imath>\textbf{(A) Triangle only}</imath> does not include the square and <imath>\textbf{(D)}</imath> does, the correct answer must be <imath>\textbf{(D)}</imath>.

Therefore, the shapes Haruki can make are the square and the triangle, and the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D) Square and triangle only}}</imath>. Conveniently, the triangle is listed last, so the shapes can be evaluated in the given order.

~jeremyq
